title: Pulse Distribution

story.briefing: Each pulse charges a whole stretch of the canopy at once. Applying them one cell at a time takes longer than the pulses themselves last.
story.success: Charge distributed. The canopy lights in a single sweep.

description: A line of `n` cells all start at 0. You are given a list of pulses, each a three-element array [l, r, v], meaning add v to every cell from index l to index r inclusive. Return the final state of all n cells. Pulses are always within bounds and l is never greater than r.
hints: Writing to every cell of every range does work proportional to the total width of all pulses. Recording only where each pulse starts and stops changing things does not.
Instead of storing values, store *changes*. A pulse of v affects the running change at exactly two positions: where it begins, and just after where it ends.
Build an array of size n + 1. For each pulse add v at index l and subtract v at index r + 1. Then sweep once from left to right keeping a running total — that total is each cell final value.
